tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use windows-sys or windows crate for safe bindings. Wrap all HANDLE in newtype with Drop impl to ensure CloseHandle is called. Use #[repr(C)] for struct layout.
tricky_patterns.risk: Memory leaks if handles not closed; ABI mismatch if struct layout wrong
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: RAII pattern: all handles owned by typed wrappers with Drop; use windows-rs metadata-driven bindings

tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Replace with clap derive macros: #[derive(Parser)] and #[arg(...)] attributes. No runtime reflection needed.
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: Use well-tested clap library; add comprehensive CLI tests

tricky_patterns.csharp_example: VirtualProtect(DispatchTablePtr, size, 0x04, out old); Marshal.WriteIntPtr(DispatchTablePtr, funcPtr);
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use windows::Win32::System::Memory::VirtualProtect in unsafe block. Document safety invariants: 1) DispatchTablePtr must be valid, 2) size must be accurate, 3) restoration required. Use ManuallyDrop and explicit restore in Drop.
tricky_patterns.risk: High - modifying system memory; could crash process or corrupt state
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Verify pointers before writing, 2) Always restore original in Drop, 3) Limit scope of unsafe, 4) Add safety comments

tricky_patterns.csharp_example: class IStreamImpl : IStream { ... }, NativeMethods.CoUnmarshalInterface(new IStreamImpl(stm), ref iid, out ppv);
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use windows-rs COM support: #[implement(IStream)] macro. Implement vtable methods. Use ComInterface trait for safe QueryInterface.
tricky_patterns.risk: Memory safety - COM uses manual reference counting; incorrect AddRef/Release causes leaks or use-after-free
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Use windows-rs ComPtr and Interface wrappers, 2) Never manually call AddRef/Release, 3) Test with ASAN/MSAN if possible

tricky_patterns.csharp_example: Thread pipeServerThread = new Thread(PipeServer); systemIdentity shared between threads
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use Arc<Mutex<Option<WindowsIdentity>>> for shared token. Use parking_lot::Mutex for performance. Return Result from thread, handle with JoinHandle.
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Rust Send/Sync bounds prevent data races at compile time, 2) Use scoped threads when possible, 3) Keep critical sections small

tricky_patterns.csharp_example: throw new Exception("No combase module found"); catch (Exception e) { ... }
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Define enum Error using thiserror: #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum GodPotatoError { #[error("No combase module found")] NoCombaseModule, ... }. Return Result<T, GodPotatoError>.
tricky_patterns.risk: None - Result is safer than exceptions
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: Use anyhow for application errors, thiserror for library errors; never use unwrap() in production paths

tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use binrw or zerocopy for declarative binary parsing with derive macros. Ensures correct endianness and alignment.
tricky_patterns.risk: Endianness bugs, alignment issues, buffer overflows
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Use binrw with #[derive(BinRead, BinWrite)], 2) Add tests with known-good byte sequences, 3) Validate lengths before allocating

tricky_patterns.pattern: Process module enumeration and memory reading
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Use windows::Win32::System::ProcessStatus::EnumProcessModules + GetModuleInformation. Read memory with ReadProcessMemory or, for current process, std::slice::from_raw_parts in unsafe.
tricky_patterns.risk: Reading unmapped memory causes access violation
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Validate module bounds before reading, 2) Handle errors gracefully, 3) Use VirtualQuery to check memory protection

tricky_patterns.pattern: Sunday pattern matching algorithm on binary data
tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Port Sunday algorithm or use memchr/aho-corasick crate for optimized pattern matching. Return Vec<usize>.
tricky_patterns.risk: Out-of-bounds access if not careful with indices
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Use safe slicing with .get(), 2) Add unit tests with edge cases (pattern at start, end, not found), 3) Consider using memchr for single-byte patterns

tricky_patterns.rust_mitigation: Define extern "system" fn type, use std::mem::transmute or raw function pointers. Store in struct to keep alive (prevent GC equivalent).
tricky_patterns.risk: Calling convention mismatch, dangling function pointers
tricky_patterns.defensive_strategy: 1) Explicitly annotate calling convention, 2) Keep closure/fn alive for lifetime of hook, 3) Document ABI assumptions

prioritized_files.rationale: Self-contained binary parsing logic, no external dependencies except standard library. Good test target for establishing binary serialization patterns.
Independent CLI parsing, replaced entirely by clap. Quick win to establish project structure.
Small wrapper, depends on COM but simple API. Tests COM setup.
COM interface implementation. Depends on ObjRef completion for testing. Validates windows-rs COM patterns.
FFI declarations, straightforward but tedious. Needed by multiple modules.
Core Windows token operations. Large file, split into manageable chunks. Start with struct definitions and simple helpers.
Process creation with multiple fallback strategies. Depends on token operations.
DCOM trigger logic. Depends on ObjRef, IStreamImpl, UnmarshalDCOM.
Pattern matching utility, independent. Can be unit tested easily.
Most complex: memory manipulation, RPC hooking, threading. Requires all previous components.
Final integration, orchestrates all components. Last piece.

platform_isolation_strategy.cfg_gating: Use #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] on Windows-only modules. Provide stub implementations or compile-time errors for Linux.
platform_isolation_strategy.rationale: Core exploit is Windows-only; args and error handling can compile on all platforms for development convenience

security_hardening_notes.principle_1_minimal_privileges: Tool requires SeImpersonatePrivilege to function (by design). Document required privileges in README. Do not request additional privileges.
security_hardening_notes.principle_2_input_validation: Validate all binary inputs (OBJREF parsing) to prevent buffer overflows. Use binrw's validation features.
security_hardening_notes.principle_3_memory_safety: Use RAII for all HANDLEs. Never use mem::forget. Minimize unsafe blocks and document safety invariants.
security_hardening_notes.principle_4_error_handling: Never unwrap() in production code paths. Use ? operator and proper Result propagation.
security_hardening_notes.principle_5_auditability: Use tracing for structured logging. Log: module load addresses, RPC hook installation, pipe connections, token captures, process creation. Levels: info for normal flow, warn for anomalies, error for failures.
security_hardening_notes.principle_6_no_evasion: Do not implement: anti-debugging, VM detection, EDR evasion, log clearing, timestomping, or any detection-avoidance techniques. This is a research tool for authorized testing only.
